stem:
The diagram shows parallel lines $p$ and $q$ cut by transversal $t$. Angle $a=110^{\circ}$. Angle $x$ is marked between the parallels.

Which claim about angle $x$ is correct?

options.text: Angle $x$ equals $70^{\circ}$, from the linear pair with angle $a$ and then equal alternate angles on the parallel lines.
Report the words parallel lines as the measure of angle $x$.
Angle $x$ equals $70^{\circ}$, and that is only the angle next to angle $a$ on the straight line.
Angle $x$ equals $110^{\circ}$, the printed measure of angle $a$.

teacher.key_rationale: Angle a and the upper interior angle form a linear pair, so that interior angle is 70°. Angle x is alternate to that interior angle on parallel lines p and q, so x=70°. Naming parallel lines as a measure, stopping at the linear pair, or copying 110° each miss the chained relationships.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote IGCSE triangle source into a two-parallel multi-step transversal figure.
